question: Does reciprocity force the new-prime ramification vector of every Selmer class to be either zero or all ones?
checks: Use the exact test space of inherited classes locally admissible away from the newly bad primes, including the real place.
Verify on every retained complete local point-image basis that ramification has one local bit and its pairing with an unramified anchor class is the known root character.
Compute the kernel of the resulting global reciprocity equations on ramification bits.
Distinguish a one-dimensional upper bound from exact realization by an already certified new affine Selmer class.
failure_semantics: This constrains the ramification quotient of the full Selmer group, not its total dimension or the Mordell-Weil rank.
